[list-style:none] min-w-0 shrink"><a class="vp-raw transition-colors hover:text-(--Labels-Primary) whitespace-nowrap" href="/en/blog/"><span class="block overflow-hidden min-w-0 whitespace-nowrap shrink text-ellipsis">Research</span></a></li></ol></nav></div><section class="pb-20 w-full"><div class="max-w-none markdown"><h1 node="[object Object]">Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence</h1>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Update(0905)</strong>：We have an updated weight that enhances <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">agentic coding</strong> and supports <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">256K context</strong>，<a href="https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Instruct-0905" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">see here</a></p>
<p>Kimi K2 is our latest Mixture-of-Experts model with 32 billion activated parameters and 1 trillion total parameters. It achieves state-of-the-art performance in frontier knowledge, math, and coding among non-thinking models. But it goes further — meticulously optimized for agentic tasks, Kimi K2 does not just answer; it acts.</p>
<p>And now, it is within your reach. Today, we are open-sourcing:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Kimi-K2-Base:</strong> The foundation model, a strong start for researchers and builders who want full control for fine-tuning and custom solutions.</li>
<li><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Kimi-K2-Instruct:</strong> The post-trained model best for drop-in, general-purpose chat and agentic experiences. It is a reflex-grade model without long thinking.</li>
</ul>
<p>With Kimi K2, advanced agentic intelligence is more open and accessible than ever. We can&#x27;t wait to see what you build.</p>
<!--$?--><div class="my-4 min-h-[160px] animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)"></div><!--/$-->
<h3 node="[object Object]">Use cases</h3>
<p>Give Kimi K2 your tools and describe your task.</p>
<p>It automatically understands how to use the tools and gets the job done. You don&#x27;t have to write any complex workflow for agentic applications.</p>
<!--$?--><div class="my-4 min-h-[160px] animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)"></div><!--/$-->
<p>Imagine using Kimi K2 to explore remote-work salaries with the Salary Data Analysis example, where 16 IPython calls generate stats, visualizations, and an interactive webpage of insights. Dive into the Stanford NLP Genealogy, and get Kimi K2 to generate an interactive site built through 5 web searches, 4 browsings, 3 clicks, 5 scrolls, 6 edits, and 2 deployments. Or plan your dream Coldplay Tour 2025 in London with Kimi K2, it crafted the plan for you through 17 seamless tool calls spanning search, calendar, Gmail, flights, Airbnb, and restaurant bookings.</p>
<p> </p>
<p>Bring Kimi K2 to your command line. It edits files. It runs commands.</p>
<p>Kimi K2 understands your environment, decides what actions to take, and executes them seamlessly.</p>
<!--$?--><div class="my-4 min-h-[160px] animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)"></div><!--/$-->
<p>For clarity, the terminal displays only a summary of each trajectory. In every example, Kimi K2 orchestrates multiple tools and commands behind the scenes to accomplish complex objectives. For instance, Kimi K2 can automate Minecraft development in JavaScript: it manages rendering, runs and debugs test cases, captures logs on failure, and iteratively improves the code until all tests succeed. For pre/post norm analysis, Kimi K2 uses the Weights &amp; Biases (wandb) data reader to extract insights from language model experiments and generates a polished analysis report. When converting a Flask project to Rust, Kimi K2 systematically refactors the codebase and runs performance benchmarks to ensure robust results.</p>
<h3 node="[object Object]">Benchmarking Kimi K2</h3>
<!--$?--><div class="my-4 min-h-[160px] animate-pulse rounded-xl bg-(--Fills-F2)"></div><!--/$-->
<h3 node="[object Object]">Open Agentic Intelligence</h3>
<p>Pre-training is the crucial foundation for <a href="https://ysymyth.github.io/The-Second-Half/" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Agentic Intelligence</a>, establishing the priors that makes reinforcement learning (RL) exploration tractable, efficient, and generalizable. However, as Ilya Sutskever also observes, human data is a finite &quot;fossil fuel&quot;, and its growth is lagging far behind the pace of compute. This makes <strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">token efficiency</strong> during pre-training a new critical coefficient in the AI scaling laws.</p>
<p>Post-training is pivotal in the &quot;<a href="https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/Era-of-Experience%20/The%20Era%20of%20Experience%20Paper.pdf" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Era of Experience</a>&quot; (David Silver, Richard Sutton, 2025). In this era, LLMs increasingly learn from their own self-generated interactions, receiving rewards that free them from the limits of human data and enable them to surpass human capabilities.</p>
<p>Kimi K2 is forged from these very insights.</p>
<h4 node="[object Object]">MuonClip Optimizer</h4>
<p>Without rigor, given an approximately finite pretraining dataset and a fixed model configuration, a more token-efficient optimizer generates more intelligence. Our previous work <a href="https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Moonlight" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Moonlight</a> has demonstrated that the <a href="https://kellerjordan.github.io/posts/muon/" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Muon</a> optimizer substantially outperforms the widely-used AdamW optimizer for LLM training.</p>
<p>Kimi K2 was designed to further scale up Moonlight, which employs an architecture similar to DeepSeek-V3. Based on scaling-law analysis, we reduce the number of heads for long-context efficiency, and increase MoE sparsity for greater token efficiency. While scaling up, we encountered a persistent challenge: training instability caused by exploding attention logits, an issue that occurs more frequently with Muon but less with AdamW in our experiments. Existing solutions such as logit soft-capping and query-key normalization were found inadequate.</p>
<p>To address this, we introduce the MuonClip optimizer that improves Muon with our proposed qk-clip technique. Specifically, qk-clip stabilizes training by directly rescaling the weight matrices of the query and key projections after Muon updates, thus controlling the scale of attention logits at the source. Concretely, the query and key projections are scaled as follows:</p>

<p>where <span class="katex"><span class="katex-mathml"><math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math></span><span class="katex-html" aria-hidden="true"><span class="base"><span class="strut" style="height:0.6151em"></span><span class="mord mathnormal">t</span></span></span></span> is a pre-set threshold. This is a general technique that can be possibly applied to other stabilization use cases.</p>
<p>Our experiments show that MuonClip effectively prevents logit explosions while maintaining downstream task performance. In practice, Kimi K2 was pre-trained on 15.5T tokens using MuonClip with zero training spike, demonstrating MuonClip as a robust solution for stable, large-scale LLM training.</p>
<div class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__imageGridContainer" style="max-width:780px;margin:0 auto"><div class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__imageGrid" style="gap:16px"><img src="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/4/2026-07-13/d9af7sff2ena62011o2g?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1" alt="Training loss vs tokens: Muon vs AdamW" loading="lazy" class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__gridImage" style="flex:1;max-width:100%"/></div></div>
<h4 node="[object Object]">Agentic Capabilities</h4>
<p>The enhanced agentic capabilities of Kimi K2 originate from two important aspects — large-scale agentic data synthesis and general reinforcement learning.</p>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">Large-Scale Agentic Data Synthesis for Tool Use Learning:</strong> To teach the model sophisticated tool-use capabilities, we developed a comprehensive pipeline inspired by ACEBench that simulates real-world tool-using scenarios at scale. Our approach systematically evolves hundreds of domains containing thousands of tools—including both real MCP (Model Context Protocol) tools and synthetic ones—then generates hundreds of agents with diverse tool sets.</p>
<p>All tasks are rubric-based, enabling consistent evaluation. Agents interact with simulated environments and user agents, creating realistic multi-turn tool-use scenarios. An LLM judge evaluates simulation results against task rubrics, filtering for high-quality training data. This scalable pipeline generates diverse, high-quality data, paving the way for large-scale rejection sampling and reinforcement learning.</p>
<div class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__imageGridContainer"><div class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__imageGrid" style="gap:16px"><img src="https://kimi-file.kimi.ai/prod-chat-kimi/kfs/4/4/2026-07-13/d9af7svf2ena62011o3g?x-tos-process=image%2Fauto-orient%2C1%2Fstrip%2Fignore-error%2C1" alt="Kimi K2 agentic data synthesis workflow" loading="lazy" class="ImageGrid-module__EsMeTG__gridImage" style="flex:1;max-width:100%"/></div></div>
<p><strong class="font-semibold text-(--Labels-Primary)">General Reinforcement Learning:</strong> The key challenge is to apply RL to tasks with both verifiable and non-verifiable rewards; typical examples of verifiable tasks are math and competition coding, while writing a research report is usually viewed as non-verifiable. Going beyond verifiable rewards, our general RL system uses a self-judging mechanism where the model acts as its own critic, providing scalable, rubric-based feedback for non-verifiable tasks.</p>
<p>Meanwhile, on-policy rollouts with verifiable rewards are used to continuously update the critic so that the critic keeps improving its evaluation accuracy on the latest policy. This can be viewed as a way of using verifiable rewards to improve the estimation of non-verifiable rewards.</p>
<h3 node="[object Object]">Getting started with Kimi K2</h3>
<h4 node="[object Object]">Try Kimi K2 on <a href="/en" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">kimi.com</a></h4>
<p>Starting today, Kimi users on web and mobile can select and use the new Kimi K2 model for free. At this moment, our MCP features for web and app are still in development. We hope to begin rolling them out in the coming weeks. In the meantime, you’re welcome to try our Researcher for an early look at its agentic capabilities. Please note that vision features are not supported for Kimi K2 yet.</p>
<h4 node="[object Object]">Use Kimi K2 with API</h4>
<p>The Kimi Platform offers an OpenAI/Anthropic compatible interface, allowing for easy adaptation of your existing applications to Kimi K2. We encourage developers to explore our tool calling API for building agent applications. For detailed information, visit <a href="https://platform.kimi.com/" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_self">platform.kimi.com</a>.</p>
<h4 node="[object Object]">Serve Kimi K2 on your own</h4>
<p>We recommend running Kimi K2 on one of the following inference engines: vLLM, SGLang, KTransformers, or TensorRT-LLM. For detailed deployment instructions, please see our <a href="https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-K2?tab=readme-ov-file#4-deployment" class="text-(--Colors-KMBlue) hover:underline" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">GitHub repository</a>.</p>
<h4 node="[object Object]">What&#x27;s next</h4>
<p>While Kimi K2 serves as a strong foundation for open agentic intelligence, a general agent uses more advanced capabilities such as thinking and visual understanding. We plan to add these to Kimi K2 in the future.</p>
<h4 node="[object Object]">Limitations</h4>
<p>In our internal tests, we&#x27;ve identified some limitations in current Kimi K2 models. When dealing with hard reasoning tasks or unclear tool definition, the model may generate excessive tokens, sometimes leading to truncated outputs or incomplete tool calls. Additionally, performance may decline on certain tasks if tool use is enabled. When building complete software projects, one-shot prompting yields performance degradation compared to using K2 under an agentic framework. We are working to address these issues in future releases and looking forward to more feedbacks.</p></div></section></div></div><!--$--><!--/$--></main><footer id="site-footer" class="bg-[#121212]"
